clue.text: Quote's about right to express contrary principles

indicators.note: the quote has the next word about it, so it wraps around that word

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it
R is the standard abbreviation for right

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so this word is read from the end back to the start

parts.note: to air a view is to express it

explanation.surface: Someone cites a source to argue for opposing principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like part of the quoting story, but it is the verb to air, a view voiced openly.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or rules by which things are judged, much as principles are.

clue.text: American girl has to cut and run

parts.note: gal is a chiefly American informal word for a girl
to lop is to cut off a branch

explanation.surface: An American girl is forced to cut and run, fleeing in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut and run' reads as one idiom, but 'cut' is wordplay and 'run' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's fastest pace is a gallop, and to gallop is to move or race quickly.

clue.text: Wedding shower?

parts.note: surface reading: a party held for a bride before the wedding, or rain on the day
setter's reading: something that falls in a shower over the couple as they leave the church

explanation.walkthrough: A wedding shower is a pre-wedding gift party in America; here it is the paper scraps thrown over the newly-weds.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are traditionally thrown over bride and groom, falling on them like rain.

clue.text: Travels around island making films

indicators.note: the travelling word goes around the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: to travel is to move
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Someone tours an island shooting films on location.
explanation.definitionFit: Movies is the everyday, chiefly American word for motion pictures or cinema films.

clue.text: Current second XI's keeping beginner in reserve

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: the team has something in its keeping, so it holds that letter inside

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: first letter of the word reserve

explanation.surface: A second-string eleven has a novice kept in reserve on the bench.
explanation.walkthrough: S then TEAM with R inside gives S + TE(R)AM.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flow of water or air moving in one direction, just as a current is.

clue.text: Captured Devizes but not very artfully

indicators.note: done artfully, the remaining letters are cleverly rearranged into a new order
the town's name is taken except for one letter, which is left out

parts.note: the Wiltshire market town, taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: An army took the town of Devizes, though without much skill.
explanation.walkthrough: Devizes is a market town in Wiltshire, England. Remove V and rearrange the other six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to take hold of by force, so seized and captured are past-tense synonyms.

clue.text: Almost not in time to get award

indicators.note: one piece sits in the other, placed inside the period of time

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: almost the whole word means it stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone nearly misses the deadline for collecting a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not in time' reads as being late, but 'almost not' is the shortened word placed inside the unit of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An honour is a title or decoration conferred for merit, such as a knighthood or medal.

clue.text: Gone off and fled with police in pursuit

indicators.note: something in pursuit follows behind, so the police piece comes after the first

parts.note: to flee is to run away
the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A suspect has gone off and run, with the detectives chasing after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone off' looks like part of the escape story but describes spoiled food. CID is the detective branch of a British police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Butter or fat that has turned stale and smells foul is rancid, the same as food that has spoiled.

clue.text: Question students interrupting angrier assembly and arguing

parts.note: QU is a standard abbreviation for question

indicators.note: the students break into the middle of the other word, sitting inside it
an assembly puts parts together into a new structure, so these letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging
L for learner, as on a British learner driver's plate, twice for plural

explanation.surface: Angry students disrupt a school assembly with questions and arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plate a British learner driver displays; two of them make students.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarrelling means having an angry dispute, which is exactly what arguing is.

clue.text: Trump is to legitimise carrying a handgun

indicators.note: the words before carry the answer inside them, running across the gaps

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the next three

explanation.surface: A politician moves to legalise carrying a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit in trumP IS TO Legitimise.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small firearm designed to be held and fired in one hand.

clue.text: Drop Facebook contact with a French pal

parts.note: un is the French for a
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: Someone removes a French friend from their social media list.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfriend someone is to remove them from your contacts on a social networking site.

clue.text: Northern river Don

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a river in north-east England flowing through Durham to Sunderland
second meaning: to put on clothes

explanation.walkthrough: The Don is itself a river in northern England (and Scotland), but here it is the verb to don, to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear clothes is to have them on, and to don is to put them on; the river flows through Durham.

clue.text: Robber's main vehicle?

parts.note: surface reading: the getaway car a thief mostly uses
setter's reading: main means the open sea, so this is a sea robber's craft

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the high seas, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneers who rob at sea sail in their own armed vessel, which is the vehicle of the seafaring thief.

clue.text: Force to have faith in fantasy

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
to believe in something is to have faith in it

explanation.surface: Someone is compelled to trust in an illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-believe is pretending or imagining, the stuff of daydreams and children's play.

clue.text: Replace old coins?

parts.note: ex means former
loose coins are small change

explanation.surface: Someone trades in out-of-date currency for new money.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests swapping obsolete coins; read as ex-change, former coins.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange one thing is to give it up and take another in its place, which is to swap or substitute it.

clue.text: Country dweller has bad time imprisoned by the old queen

indicators.note: something imprisoned is held inside walls, here inside the royal letters

parts.note: Victoria Regina, the royal cipher of Queen Victoria
ill means bad, as in ill effects
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rustic does a hard spell of prison time under Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Regina's royal cipher is still seen on old British post boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A villager lives in a small rural settlement, so is a dweller in the countryside.

clue.text: Animal cries from sow suffering after farrow

indicators.note: the rearranged piece comes after the other, placed second in the answer

parts.note: Mia is the name that comes before Farrow, the American actress

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A sow cries out in pain after giving birth to a litter of piglets.
explanation.walkthrough: A farrow is a litter of pigs, but here it is Mia Farrow, the film actress: the word that comes before Farrow is MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Miaows are the sounds a cat makes, so they are cries uttered by an animal.

clue.text: Work to tile WC

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: A builder's job is to tile the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: WC stands for water closet, a polite British term for a lavatory.

clue.text: Struggle for fellows in charge last month engaged in do-it-yourself

indicators.note: pieces engaged in an activity are inside it, so they sit within the letters that follow

parts.note: the usual abbreviation for do-it-yourself
F for fellow, doubled for the plural
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge
ult., ultimo, is the old business abbreviation for last month

explanation.surface: Some fellows put in charge of home improvements last month are struggling.
explanation.walkthrough: Ultimo is old commercial-letter Latin for 'of last month', abbreviated in letters such as 'your letter of the 5th ult.'
explanation.definitionFit: A difficulty is a problem or hardship, something that has to be struggled with.

clue.text: Financed and established with nothing lacking

indicators.note: a word lacking something has had it taken away, so a letter goes missing

parts.note: to found an institution is to establish it
O is the shape of zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A business that was paid for and set up without anything missing.
explanation.walkthrough: FOUNDED loses its O to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something funded has been provided with money, so it is financed.

clue.text: Certainly solver is tense!

parts.note: the solver is the person reading the clue, addressed as you
is is a form of the verb to be
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: The setter teases that the solver is certainly feeling nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous, but it gives the grammar abbreviation T.
explanation.definitionFit: You bet is an informal exclamation of emphatic agreement, meaning of course or definitely.

clue.text: Appear to have left love with broken heart

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word broken

explanation.surface: Someone who has lost in love looks heartbroken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken heart' reads as one phrase, but broken is the word whose middle is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: To look happy is to seem or appear happy, so look and appear share this sense.

clue.text: Fine high hilltop's not visible in spring

indicators.note: if the top of the hill cannot be seen, its first letter is missing

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
a mountain is a very high hill

explanation.surface: On a clear day a hill's summit is hidden in spring mist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hill' does double duty: with 'high' it is the word, and its top is what goes missing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fountain is a natural spring of water rising from the ground, or its source.

clue.text: Not qualified to analyse nebula

indicators.note: to analyse is to break into parts, so these letters are split up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, before rearranging

explanation.surface: An amateur lacks the expertise to study a cloud of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unable to do a task lacks the ability or competence, so is not qualified for it.

clue.text: Toboggan takes bend on side rim

indicators.note: one piece sits right on, next to, the following piece

parts.note: an S-bend is shaped like the letter S
a ledge is a narrow rim or shelf projecting from a side wall

explanation.surface: A sledge rider takes a corner riding up on the edge of the track.
explanation.definitionFit: A toboggan is a long, low sled for sliding downhill over snow, a kind of sledge.

clue.text: Refuse to take soldiers by plane over Cuba

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: the plane goes over and around the island, enclosing it

parts.note: a jet is a kind of plane
C is the international vehicle code for Cuba

explanation.surface: Soldiers decline to fly over Cuba by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps; C, Cuba's code, sits inside JET.
explanation.definitionFit: To reject something is to decline or turn it down, the same as refusing it.
